title: llmao Shell Plugin Launches: Type Prompts in Terminal
summary: New open-source shell plugin llmao intercepts command errors and routes natural language prompts to Claude Code and Codex agents. Available now on GitHub.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Open-source shell plugin llmao lets developers type natural language coding prompts directly in terminal, routing them to Claude Code or Codex agents automatically.
- Plugin intercepts command-not-found errors, checks for typos first, then treats unrecognized input as AI agent prompts while preserving normal shell commands.
- Officially launched on November 22, 2026, with source code available on GitHub for immediate installation and customization by development teams.


Developers can now type natural language coding instructions directly into their terminal shell, thanks to llmao, a new open-source plugin that intercepts command errors and routes them to AI coding agents. The tool bridges the gap between traditional command-line workflows and conversational AI interfaces, letting users issue prompts like "work on the next task in PLAN.md" without leaving their terminal environment.


## How the Shell Plugin Works


The llmao plugin sits between the shell and the user's input stream, monitoring for command-not-found errors. When the shell encounters an unrecognized command, llmao performs a two-step evaluation: first checking whether the input resembles a typo of a known command (like "gti" instead of "git"), then treating genuinely unrecognized input as a natural language prompt for coding agents.


Regular commands continue to execute normally. A developer typing "git status" sees standard Git output, while "work on the authentication module" triggers[Claude Code](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-code-vs-codex) or Codex in the current directory. This design preserves existing muscle memory while adding conversational capabilities to the command line.


## Motivation and Development Origins


Developer mquan built llmao after repeatedly entering coding instructions into the shell by mistake, a common friction point when switching between chat interfaces and terminal windows. The plugin emerged from this workflow pain point, transforming accidental behavior into a productive feature. By catching these "mistakes" and redirecting them to appropriate AI agents, llmao turns a user error into an intentional interaction pattern.


The typo detection layer prevents false positives. Without this safeguard, common command misspellings would trigger AI agent sessions instead of helpful suggestions. The plugin's intelligence lies in distinguishing between probable typos (single character transpositions, omissions) and genuine natural language prompts.


## Integration with Claude Code and Codex


The plugin supports multiple coding agents, including Claude Code and GitHub Codex. When llmao identifies a natural language prompt, it launches the appropriate agent in the current working directory, maintaining context about the project structure and existing files. Users can configure which agent to invoke by default, or use command prefixes to specify an agent for individual prompts.


This terminal integration complements existing IDE extensions and standalone agent interfaces. Developers working primarily in the command line no longer need to switch to a browser tab or separate application to request AI assistance. The workflow remains inside the terminal environment, reducing context switching and preserving focus.


## Release Details and Availability


Officially launched on November 22, 2026, llmao is available as an open-source project on GitHub. The repository includes installation instructions for common shells (bash, zsh, fish) and configuration options for customizing agent selection, timeout behavior, and typo detection sensitivity. Early adopters on Hacker News reported successful integration with existing dotfiles and shell configurations.


The plugin requires API access to supported coding agents. Users need valid credentials for Claude Code or Codex to route prompts successfully. Installation involves adding a source line to shell configuration files and setting environment variables for agent endpoints.


## What This Means for Terminal Workflows


llmao represents a shift toward ambient AI assistance in developer tools. Rather than requiring explicit mode switching to interact with coding agents, the plugin embeds conversational capabilities directly into the command-line environment developers already inhabit. This pattern could extend to other terminal-based workflows, from system administration to data analysis, where natural language instructions complement traditional commands. The open-source release invites experimentation and adaptation across different use cases and agent platforms.
